title: Make backtest evidence postdate decisions and validate each citation
summary: Fix three root causes in 'athena backtest'. (1) Take D87's start from the git history of its text in docs/decisions.md and count only later records. (2) Derive a host-refused merge only when the text ties the HTTP code to the refused merge. (3) Validate every citation against the signal's fields and time window, and fail on any invalid one. Report the real-records result either way.

defaults_applied.how: New tests cover each of the three fixes; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Fixes the three causes, not the single D87 case.
The real-records run of the backtest is exercised and its result reported.
One focused change in the backtest and the derivation.
Recovered the structure from backtest.rs, watcher.rs and the test fixtures.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The decision start time comes from running `git log` over the repository's own history at run time. Tests build temporary git repos or inject the start time.
The start is the first commit that added the entry's text (D87: 383edca, 2026-10-13T19:21Z), not a later amendment. Only strictly later records count.
I could not read the real records or the git history here, so the expected real result is taken from the request and not measured.
The derivation is narrow: the HTTP code and a refused merge must be tied in one sentence or clause, and wording about opening a PR excludes it.

acceptance_criteria.text: backtest.rs gets each decision's start time from the git history of the decision's text in docs/decisions.md. For D87 that is the commit that introduced the entry. Only host-error and intervention records dated after that start are counted by the signals. The start time is a field of the report.

derive_host_error derives a refusal only when the text ties an HTTP code to the refused merge itself. A bare occurrence of 'merge', 'merges' or 'merged' no longer suffices. When unsure it returns None.

The backtest validates each cited record (observed host-error, derived record with its source intervention, and intervention): it matches the signal's fields and falls inside the signal's time window, meaning it postdates the decision's start. Any invalid citation adds a Finding and makes Report::passed() false. The old checks of counts and id existence remain.
The citation check also covers the derived record's source intervention and the introspection record's intervention. An introspection whose triggering event predates the decision is a finding.

Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets`. Both pass. New tests cover: a record before the decision start is not counted; an intervention that mentions 'merged' in the sense of opening a pull request, with HTTP 422, derives nothing; a text that ties HTTP 422 or 405 to the refused merge derives a record; an invalid citation fails the backtest.

Run `cargo run -- backtest` on the real records. D87 is under review citing only ar1x, both directly and through its derived record. The introspection record names ar1x's event. Nothing else is flagged. The kn3q and qk2d interventions are not cited. The actual output is reported, even if it differs.

out_of_scope: Changing D87 or D88 text, or docs/decisions.md and docs/decision-links.toml
Editing records/ or writing derived records to disk
Adding signals or decisions beyond D87 and D88
Changing governance files such as athena.toml, defaults.toml, CI workflows or lint configuration
departures: This is multi-part work across two crates: a git-history lookup, a stricter derivation and citation validation. The expected real-records result also cannot be confirmed here. Cost, time and verification odds are adjusted for that from the reference.
